citation: Office of Management and Budget (eCFR, National Archives). 2 CFR 200.340 Termination. 2024-04-22. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.340
title: 2 CFR 200.340 Termination
publisher: Office of Management and Budget (eCFR, National Archives)
summary: The termination section of the Uniform Guidance as in force on 2026-10-04. It lists four ways an award may be ended, requires termination provisions to be stated in the award terms, and requires a termination for material non-compliance to be reported in SAM.gov.
why_it_mattered: The section that lists the ways an award may be ended early. The 2025 terminations and the suits over them were argued on its fourth ground, and the 2026 proposed rewrite would change it.
key_facts: Four grounds: (1) failure to comply with the terms and conditions; (2) with the consent of the recipient; (3) by the recipient on written notification; (4) pursuant to the terms and conditions of the award.
Paragraph (a)(4) includes termination, to the extent authorized by law, if an award no longer effectuates the program goals or agency priorities.
Paragraph (b): the agency or pass-through entity must clearly and unambiguously specify all termination provisions in the terms and conditions of the award.
Paragraph (c): a termination for material failure to comply must be reported in SAM.gov, entered through CPARS.
Paragraph (d): after termination both sides remain responsible for closeout (200.344) and post-closeout adjustments (200.345).
eCFR page shown as up to date as of 10/01/2026; section source 89 FR 30136, Apr. 22, 2024.
eCFR banner: up to date as of 10/01/2026; title 2 last amended 8/17/2026.
Source note: 89 FR 30136, Apr. 22, 2024.

Paragraph (a) has four grounds: failure to comply with the terms and conditions; with the consent of the recipient or subrecipient; by the recipient or subrecipient on written notification; and by the agency or pass-through entity pursuant to the terms and conditions of the award, including if an award no longer effectuates the program goals or agency priorities.
Paragraph (b): agencies must clearly and unambiguously specify all termination provisions in the terms and conditions of the award.

Paragraph (c): a termination for material noncompliance is reported in SAM.gov through CPARS only after the recipient has exhausted its opportunities to object or 30 calendar days have passed without notice of an appeal.
Paragraph (d): both sides remain responsible for closeout under 200.344 and 200.345.

citation: Office of Management and Budget (eCFR, National Archives). 2 CFR 200.414 Indirect costs. 2024-04-22. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.414
title: 2 CFR 200.414 Indirect costs
publisher: Office of Management and Budget (eCFR, National Archives)
summary: The governing section on indirect (facilities and administrative) costs. It requires every federal agency to accept a negotiated rate, states the two exceptions, sets the de minimis rate at up to 15 percent of modified total direct costs, and allows a one-time extension of a negotiated rate for up to four years.
why_it_mattered: The section that sets how indirect costs are paid on a federal award. It makes a negotiated rate binding on every agency, and gives an organisation without one the de minimis rate of up to 15 percent, the first of the two "fifteen percents" a newcomer hears about.
key_facts: Negotiated indirect cost rates must be accepted by all Federal agencies (200.414(c)(1)).
A different rate may be used for a class of awards or a single award only when required by Federal statute or regulation, or when approved by the awarding agency under paragraph (c)(3).

The agency must notify OMB of any approved deviations (c)(2), make its deviation policies and criteria publicly available (c)(3), and state its indirect cost policies in the notice of funding opportunity (c)(4).
Pass-through entities must accept all federally negotiated indirect cost rates for subrecipients (200.414(d)).
De minimis rate: up to 15 percent of MTDC, for recipients and subrecipients without a current Federal negotiated rate; no documentation is required to justify it (200.414(f)).
One-time extension of a current negotiated rate for up to four years, subject to approval of the cognizant agency for indirect costs (200.414(g)).
eCFR page shown as up to date as of 10/01/2026; section source 89 FR 30136, Apr. 22, 2024.
eCFR banner: up to date as of 10/01/2026; title 2 last amended 8/17/2026.
Source note at the end of the section: 89 FR 30136, Apr. 22, 2024.
Paragraph (c): negotiated indirect cost rates must be accepted by all Federal agencies; a different rate needs a statute, a regulation or an approved deviation, with notice to OMB.
Paragraph (f): a de minimis rate of up to 15 percent of modified total direct costs (MTDC); no documentation; may be used indefinitely.
Paragraph (g): a one-time extension of a current negotiated rate agreement for up to four years.

summary: The same proposed rule in govinfo's text and PDF renditions, which the fetch read as far as the discussion of section 200.111 (page 32210). OMB proposes to issue the requirements as regulation, removing the statement in 2 CFR 1.105 that the text is guidance, not regulation; it cites 31 U.S.C. 503 and 31 U.S.C. 6307.

200.305: Federal agencies and pass-through entities would require a justification for payment requests; the PDF excerpt also names Treasury's Do Not Pay system.
200.329-200.332: pass-through entities to report subawards on SAM.gov; the preamble refers to the retirement of FSRS.gov on March 8, 2025.

200.340: would clarify agencies' ability to terminate discretionary awards for discretionary reasons consistent with law; proposed 200.101(d)(2) would make subpart F and 200.340 govern non-statutory conflicts with agency regulations.

title: 2 CFR 200.101 Applicability (annual edition revised as of January 1, 2025)
publisher: Office of Management and Budget (Code of Federal Regulations, govinfo)
summary: States which subparts of Part 200 apply to which kinds of award and which programmes are carved out. Read in the January 1, 2025 annual edition on govinfo because eCFR was rate-limited.
why_it_mattered: The applicability section. It says which parts of the Uniform Guidance reach which awards, that award terms flow down to subawards, and that a statute governs where it conflicts with the part.
key_facts: Subparts A and B apply to all Federal financial assistance; subparts C and D to grants and cooperative agreements; subpart E (cost principles) does not apply to fixed amount awards (with limited exceptions), food commodities, loans or awards to hospitals.
Subpart F (audit) applies to grants and cooperative agreements including fixed amount awards, cost-type contracts under the FAR, loans and other assistance under the Single Audit Act.
Terms and conditions of Federal awards flow down to subawards unless a section or the award terms say otherwise.
Federal statutes or regulations govern where they conflict with Part 200 (paragraph (d)).

Paragraph (e): subparts C, D and E do not apply (except specified provisions) to block grants authorised by the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1981 and certain other listed programmes; paragraph (f) lists entitlement programmes outside subpart C, among them TANF, Medicaid and CHIP.
Agencies may apply subparts A to E to for-profit organizations, foreign public entities and foreign organizations where agency regulations or statute permit.
quotes: flow down to subawards to subrecipients unless a particular section of this part or the terms and conditions of the Federal award specifically indicate otherwise

summary: The government-wide rule that makes a UEI and SAM.gov registration a condition of applying for and holding federal financial assistance. It gives the exceptions, the effect of non-compliance and the lighter rule for subrecipients.
why_it_mattered: The rule that makes a Unique Entity ID and a SAM.gov registration a condition of every federal application, and the lighter rule for subrecipients. The first gate on every federal route rests on it.
key_facts: Section 25.200 requires each notice of funding opportunity to require applicants to be registered in SAM.gov before submitting, to keep the registration current while an award or application is active, and to include the UEI in each application.
Section 25.205(a) bars an agency from issuing an award, or amending one to add funds, to an entity not in compliance.

Section 25.110 lets an agency exempt an applicant or recipient for national security, for a foreign entity with an award under $25,000 performed outside the United States, or in exigent circumstances.
Section 25.300(a) bars a recipient from making a subaward to a subrecipient that has not obtained a UEI and given it to the recipient.
Section 25.400 defines the UEI as the universal identifier assigned by SAM.gov to uniquely identify an entity.
Section 25.200(b)(2) requires the applicant or recipient to review and update its SAM.gov information annually from the date of initial registration or later updates.
The part's source note is 89 FR 30109, April 22, 2024; the eCFR showed title 2 as up to date as of 10/01/2026 and last amended 8/17/2026, with no 2025 or 2026 citation on this part.
